articleTitle: A Sensing Device for Highly Efficient Real-Time Road Condition Monitoring and Drive Assistance System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: A sensing device to address traffic congestion and road accidents due to deteriorated roads, focusing on potholes and uneven surfaces, is proposed in this paper. The device is capable of real-time road condition detection when retrofitted onto vehicles. Using inertial sensors and an on-board microcontroller, the device identifies road anomalies, aiding disaster prevention by alerting drivers to take precautions and governments to take necessary action about the road conditions. The data collected from the proposed device can be used to enhance road/drive safety hence contributing to improved traffic management and reducing fatalities. The concept of the proposed device has been proven using Arduino and ESP32 microcontroller boards with sensor attachments and can be developed as a custom device for high volume and low cost.

articleTitle: TinyML Acoustic Classification using RAMAN Accelerator and Neuromorphic Cochlea
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: The growing use of acoustic classification systems in edge computing and Internet of Things (IoT) devices has created a demand for innovative technologies and methods that can deliver high performance and energy efficiency. In this work, we introduce a novel audio inference system that combines RAMAN, a Re-configurable and spArse tinyML Accelerator for infereNce, with a hardware-efficient Neuromorphic cochlea for pre-processing. The neuromorphic cochlea mimics human hearing, specifically by employing the ‘Cascade of Asymmetric Resonators (CAR)’ model to replicate the basilar membrane filter in the human cochlea. In this study, we utilize a 30 cascaded-filter cochlear section to process real-time audio data and a RAMAN classifier for audio classification. RAMAN leverages activation and weight sparsity within the neural network to reduce storage, latency, and power consumption. The proposed audio inference system has been implemented on a Microchip MPFS250T SoC field-programmable gate array (FPGA) with 52.57k LUTs, all while operating with a power consumption of 237.3 mW at 40 MHz clock frequency. The proposed audio inference system is designed for low-power auditory edge applications such as speaker verification, speech detection, and keyword spotting.

articleTitle: 35 pW, 19.23 ppm/°C Dual Self-Regulated CMOS Voltage Reference for Energy Autonomous IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: We present a picowatt CMOS voltage reference (VR) that improves the line sensitivity (LS) using a dual self-regulation circuit for energy-harvesting IoT applications. Selfregulating structures increase the effective input impedance of the power supply to suppress the supply noise coupled to the output, resulting in low LS. The proposed design has been implemented in a 65 nm CMOS low power (LP) process and occupies an active area of 1373 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The post-layout Monte Carlo simulation shows that the circuit gives an average reference voltage of 287 mV and a standard deviation of 10.32 mV. The line sensitivity is 0.59%/V across the supply voltage range from 0.5 V to 1.2 V and lower to 0.036%/V when the power supply sweeps from 0.8 V to 1.2 V, respectively. With a minimum supply of 0.5 V, the average temperature coefficient is 19.23 ppm/°C over the temperature range of 0°C to 140°C. The circuit consumes 70 pA of quiescent current from a 0.5 V supply at room temperature, resulting in 35 pW power consumption.

articleTitle: Exploring Early Timing Insights: The Impact of Parasitic Methodology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: In the pursuit of advancing integrated circuit design for smaller technology nodes, this paper introduces an innovative technique called Dummy Metal Fill (DMF). This method addresses timing challenges encountered during the fill stage, a crucial step in manufacturing that often leads to significant timing discrepancies, particularly in smaller nodes. There’s a pressing need for proactive parasitic estimation during the structural design phase to effectively mitigate these timing issues. By incorporating early RC (resistance-capacitance) calculations into the Place and Route (PNR) workflow, DMF offers a groundbreaking solution that revolutionizes current design methodologies. With the implementation of DMF, we observe enhancements in congestion and routing Design Rule Checks (DRCs), resulting in a 7.59% reduction in total power consumption. Furthermore, this strategy preserves an impressive 60% of Engineering Change Order (ECO) cycles and achieves a 99% timing accuracy rate.

articleTitle: Leveraging PolarFire SoC for Heartbeat Classification Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: Advancements in machine learning and artificial intelligence has made it possible to analyze enormous medical datasets for disease diagnosis and treatment outcomes which has changed the healthcare domain. This paper focuses on hearbeat classification for arrhythmia detection using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). It presents a CNN model trained on MITBIH arrhythmia database. The model is capable of classifying 5 different types of heartbeats. The CNN model is implemented for Microchip PolarFire SoC FPGA using VectorBlox SDK environment and evaluated for its functionality and accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhancing Linearity and Efficiency in Multi-Bit MAC Computation for Convolution in DNNs Using SRAM Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method to enhance the linearity of the multi-bit Multiply and accumulate (MAC) operation for reliable and energy-efficient convolution computation in binary-weight deep neural networks (DNNs) using static random-access memory (SRAM). We systematically analyze factors influencing linearity and inconsistency in multi-row read and write operations for analog In-Memory computation at 45 nm technology. The proposed approach employs a current mirror based approach with voltage modulated word line triggering to improve linearity in multi-bit dot product computation for MAC. With CM, linearity improves by 80% and performance analysis demonstrates a 33% enhancement in power dissipation in the proposed design.

articleTitle: FPGA Enabled Deep Learning Accelerator For Multiclass Electrocardiogram Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: The early identification and diagnosis of cardiac arrhythmias play a crucial role in preventing sudden and anticipated fatalities. An irregular heartbeat rhythm is believed to contribute to the age-related increase in arrhythmia. Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals serve as a means to detect anomalous cardiac activity. The proposed approach encompasses a comprehensive framework utilizing a deep learning algorithm for the automated identification of various irregular heartbeats within substantial ECG datasets. Given the widespread adoption of deep learning algorithms in the medical field, the focus of this study is to explore the utilization of a field programmable gate array (FPGA) in accelerating the classification of ECG signals through convolutional neural networks (CNN). The suggested design was implemented on the Libero platform, employing the Microchip PolarFire SoC Icicle Kit. Additionally, the efficacy of the proposed methodology is assessed in comparison to other existing FPGA-based classifiers, utilizing several performance indicators such as classification accuracy, precision, specificity, and sensitivity.

articleTitle: Analyzing Area and Latency Overhead in C and RTL Locked Designs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: Modern integrated circuit (IC) design hubs have adopted the fab-less design methodology for developing their System on Chips (SoCs). This allows for unreliable entities to operate at various IC supply chain nodes, posing security concerns such as IP piracy, counterfeiting, and overproduction of ICs. Logic locking is a widely accepted technique for securing modern IC designs against such threats. However, logic locking imposes additional resource constraints and introduces area and latency overhead in the original design, thereby affecting its efficiency and performance. This report analyses the area and latency overhead incurred when an original IC is locked at the behavioural level (C) and register transfer level (RTL). The design is locked to ensure uniform locking in both the C and RTL designs. Experimental results show that locking at RTL has less overhead than its equivalent locked C code.

articleTitle: Approximate Multiplier for Optimized Power and Delay
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: Approximate multipliers which allow certain level of acceptable error becomes important in many applications such as computer Vision, digital signal processing (DSP), machine learning, and artificial intelligence. This work presents an implementation of an approximate multiplier using a modified Wallace tree design that combines full adders, half adders, and 42 approximate compressors. It uses the PolarFire silicon on chipt (SoC) Icicle Kit FPGA MPFS250_ES and Libero Soc simulation software. The resulting average error percentage is found to be $\mathbf{2 1 . 9 \%}$ along with the reduction in delay by $23.94 \%$.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Super-Pipelining and Quantization for Computer Vision Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: We introduce an automated analysis platform for multi-objective super-pipelining and quantization, leveraging the Critical Path Method for system evaluation and High-Level Synthesis (HLS) for hardware integration and performance reporting. The multi-objective optimization framework based on NSGA-II algorithm finds the optimal system performance configurations. Our approach also includes a system warehousing to manage timing uncertainties. An example image recognition system with HOG hard IP and SVM soft IP is optimized as reduced slacks, lower multipliers and memory usage, while maintaining FPS efficiency and over 90% F1-score for 2K images. The platform ensures robust integration, even when recruiting IPs from different sources.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Channel Estimation on System on Chip
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: Channel estimation (CE) is crucial for reliable wireless data transmission. Recent works have shown that deep learning (DL) based CE techniques outperform the conventional least square (LS) and linear minimum mean square error (LMMSE) CE techniques. However, their effect on latency and area still to be evaluated. In this work, we introduce the hardware design of a DL-augmented CE scheme for a preamble-based OFDM system and implement it on the PolarFire System-on-chip by Microchip Technology. We also introduce a novel MATLAB-based hardware simulation and verification workflow to test hardware accelerators in end-to-end simulation environments.

articleTitle: FPGA-based Acceleration of Arrhythmia Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)

authors.preferredName: Daggupati Venkata N R Mohitananda Sanjay

abstract: The pre-processing approach for filtering electrocardiogram (ECG) data is proposed in this study, utilizing an accurate and energy-efficient VLSI architecture. The QRS complex detection is introduced through hardware based on field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). This method serves as the foundation for the majority of the suggested detection system; however, during the detection step, a straightforward and effective technique is employed. This approach is one of the simplest methods for identifying the QRS complex in ECG readings. Moreover, it has been successfully implemented using FPGA technology.

articleTitle: FPGA-targeted optimization approaches for SVM and CNN human activity recognition models using the HARTH and HAR70+ datasets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) has been explored extensively for decades as a use case of machine learning (ML) in low-power embedded applications such as FPGAs. While most existing research has focused on development of classical ML models, recent work targets deep ML models for their capacity to learn effectively on low-quality, noisy datasets. As these models have been widely developed for improved accuracy and recently produced publicly available free-living datasets such as HARTH and HAR70+ have started targeting the issue of reliable annotations, our challenge of interest is model deployment. This study explores optimization approaches specifically for resource-limited FPGA deployment applications. We evaluate their trade-offs in model performance and resource utilization estimates after high-level synthesis (HLS) of representative classical (SVM) and deep (CNN) learning models. Axis and data format reduction were most effective in balancing model performance and resource utilization with single-axis models consuming half the resources estimated for our unoptimized models.

articleTitle: A Correlation Based Adaptation (CBA) for Efficient Implementation of Golomb-Rice Encoding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: This paper presents a hardware implementation of Golomb-Rice (GR) encoding for any given geometrical distribution of the input data by utilizing a novel correlation based adaptation (CBA) approach to estimate the tunable parameter. CBA uses a decision making pixel, which uses inherent spatial and spectral correlation among previous processed neighborhood of the current pixel i.e. causal neighborhood. This allows lossless recovery of data and reduces the computational complexity by avoiding the calculation of logarithmic inequality involved in the GR encoder. Signal and Image Processing Institute (SIPI) images along with the preprocessed hyperspectral data by a simple lossless algorithm (SLA) is used to evaluate performance of the proposed CBA approach. Software implementation shows improvement in compression performance by maximum of 4.47 and 38.22% in SIPI and hyperspectral test data respectively. The hardware implementation of the proposed encoding is done on Kintex KCU-105 evaluation board with input test data of 8-bit dynamic range. With the use of efficient 3-stage pipelining in encoder and decoder, CBA based architectures work at a maximum frequency of 416 MHz, achieving a throughput of 3.3 Gbps.

articleTitle: A 4-kHz per °C High Linearity On-chip Temperature Sensor Implemented Using 40-nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: In this research, a standard TSMC 40-nm CMOS process is used to implement a highly linear and high resolution temperature sensor. It is composed of an averaging feedback operational amplifier relaxation oscillator controlled by a PTAT current generator. Post-layout simulations show a detection range of $0^{\circ} \sim 100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and a 4 kHz per °C resolution. The maximum linearity error is simulated to be 0.15% at the FF corner and 99.85% linear fit. The power consumption of the design is 0.2015 mW at the maximum output frequency $=1.57 \mathrm{MHz}$, and the area of $5291.5 \mu \mathrm{~m}^{2}$.

articleTitle: A 9-bit 2MS/s Set-and-Down Monotonic SAR ADC in 22nm-FDSOI for MEMS-based Thermoelectric Sensor Readout Interface Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: This paper discusses the design and performance of a set-and-down monotonic SAR ADC in 22nm-FDSOI. The designed 9-bit, 2MS/s SAR ADC has a simulated ENOB of 8.94 bits, SNDR of 55.57dB, SFDR of 70.10dB, and a total power consumption of 7.86μW. The achieved FoM for the SAR ADC is 8.02fJ/conv-step. The SAR ADC design is suitable as data converters for MEMS-based thermoelectric sensor readout interface circuits.

articleTitle: Implementation of Reconfigurable Deep Learning Accelerator (RDLA) on PolarFire SoC
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: In neural networks and other computationally demanding applications, general-purpose CPUs are slow and ineffective. To run such applications, it is better to create specialized hardware capable of doing several multiply-accumulate operations quickly and effectively. For a wide range of neural network applications, the Reconfigurable Deep Learning Accelerator (RDLA) architecture has been developed. The fundamental unit of the RDLA is composed of a variety of Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) units, registers, and Address Generation Units (AGU). On the PolarFire SoC, RDLA was tested and implemented with a clock frequency of up to 62.5MHz for data processing. This paper shows the results testing with different images for a custom MNIST model with 4 layers with accuracy of 97.49% with power consumption of 1.85W.

articleTitle: Digital Background Calibration Technique to Mitigate Vertical FPN in CMOS Image Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: A digital background calibration technique to mitigate vertical FPN (VFPN) in CMOS image sensors is proposed in this work. The technique takes outputs of two adjacent ADC in the column as input to LMS filter. The filter weights are updated iteratively until the difference in ADC outputs converges to a minimum. A prototype 10-bit ADC with the worst-case error of 1/2 MSB is implemented and simulated in MATLAB as a proof of concept. It is observed that the difference in ADC outputs is converged to 5e-7 from 5e-3 using hyperparameters $\mu_{e}$ and $\mu_{w}$ equal to $2^{-12}$ and $2^{-17}$, respectively.

articleTitle: ADAS Pothole Detection System using FPGA
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) have become integral to the modern automotive industry, enhancing safety and driving convenience. ADAS is pivotal, utilizing specialized algorithms for lane following, obstruction detection, and collision avoidance. Certain ADAS functionalities require hardware acceleration to achieve real-time throughput. This paper aims to demonstrate the use of hardware acceleration tools for running image processing algorithms crucial in ADAS systems. Pothole detection is a critical component of ADAS as it ensures the safety and efficiency of the vehicles. The Pothole Detection System integrates seamlessly with the car’s ADAS, capitalizing on its existing sensors and computing power. As vehicles increasingly use ADAS, these results are poised to impact the automotive industry’s ongoing pursuit of safer and smarter transportation.

articleTitle: An Energy Efficient C-2C Charge-Sharing Based Analog Compute-In-Memory Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference On Postgraduate Research In Microelectronics And Electronics (PRIMEAsia)
abstract: SRAM-based analog compute-in-memory (CIM) architecture has gained more attention due to its high energy efficiency. A C-2C charge sharing-based robust, scalable, and energy efficient multi-bit analog CIM architecture is proposed in this article. The energy consumption is 0.6 fJ for 4-bit multiplication and accumulation (MAC) operation, and the achieved energy efficiency is 1666 TOPS/W at 0.9 V supply voltage. The achieved energy efficiency is 2.6× higher than state-of-the-art. The access time for 4-bit MAC output results is 5 ns, 2× less than the reported work. The functional simulations are performed in the 28 nm CMOS technology node. A LeNet-5 CNN model is implemented using the proposed architecture, and the achieved inference accuracy is 98.6% for the MNIST data set. The figure-of-merit (FoM) of the proposed architecture is 11662, which is 33.5× higher than the state-of-the-art.
